newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - BOC H1 seen lower on stg strength.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - BOC H1 seen lower on stg strength.

text.p: British gases company BOC Group Plc is expected to report a slight decline in first half pre-tax profits on May 13, reflecting the strength of sterling and pricing weakness in the key U.S. market, market analysts said on Friday.
Analysts are predicting pre-tax profits of between 210.0 and 217.0 million stg compared with 217.4 million a year earlier.
The interim dividend is expected to rise to 14.5 pence from 13.5 pence.
Sterling's continued strength against the dollar is again seen taking the shine off an otherwise solid performance, with the core specialist gases business worst-affected.

In the three months to December 31, BOC said the pound's rise had cut profits by around seven percent. Around one third of group sales are in North and South America, with similar proportions in Europe and the Far East.
Last month, analysts at Kleinwort Benson downgraded BOC to a sell from a hold, citing a slowdown in the U.S. gases market.
BOC's shares have slipped back from a high of 10.42 stg in March, touching a low for the year of 898 pence in mid-April. BOC was up 1 1/2 pence at 969 late around midday on Friday.

Over the past 12 months, the stock has underperformed the FT-SE all share index by just above eight percent. But its niche position has protected it from the vagaries of the general chemicals market and the stock has outperformed the rest of the UK chemical sector by 17 percent, according to Reuters 3000 data.
The market will be watching for further signs of a pick-up in orders at BOC's vacuum business, which supplies specialist machinery to create super-clean environments in semi-conductor factories.
